rendered: The premise does not match the document. It does not say bare Al outperformed carbon/Al at high current. The reverse is reported. At 4 mA/cm^2[1], the carbon/Al electrode kept a voltage hysteresis of 45 mV[2]. Bare Al electrodes, by contrast, were prone to failure at these currents. The document attributes bare Al's weaker behavior to its higher nucleation overpotential, which makes plating uneven and produced signs of shorting[3]. The carbon layer lowers that barrier, with nucleation overpotential reduced from 19 to 12 mV[4]. The document does not report a hysteresis value for bare Al at 4 mA/cm^2[5], so it gives no basis for how much lower the carbon/Al hysteresis is than bare Al's. The only hysteresis comparison at that current is with earlier Cu electrodes, which reported nearly double the hysteresis at[6] 4 mA/cm^2[7]. That comparison concerns Cu, not bare Al.
